properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 29 at 4:27PM MDT until October 29 at 7:15PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern El Paso County in western Texas...

* Until 715 PM MDT.

* At 427 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Far East El Paso, Homestead Meadows and Butterfield.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

banks. Rock, mud and debris may flow into roadways and flash
flooding can not be ruled out, especially in urban areas.

* CONFIDENCE...High confidence in widespread rainfall, with low
confidence in river and flash flooding.

* WHAT...A strong Pacific storm system will interact with a
atmospheric river streaming into the Desert Southwest and Four
Corners region, producing widespread rain which will focus in
the mountains.

* WHERE...Four Corners and surrounding region, including Aztec,
Bloomfield, Farmington and Shiprock.

last week's rainfall and flooding, making additional runoff more
efficient and can more easily cause flooding problems. The
greatest precipitation amounts are forecast in the San Juan
Mountains of Colorado, which will create high flows in the
Animas and La Plata Rivers. These rivers feed the San Juan
River, which saw record flooding last week.

unfolds.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 29 at 10:53AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
ESFGJT

Low pressure begins to dig southward from the PACNW on Friday,
tapping into a fetch of Pacific moisture that will evolve into an
atmospheric river streaming into the Desert Southwest this weekend.
Showers and thunderstorms develop on Friday and Saturday across the
region. Lighter rainfall totals Friday and Saturday will reflect,
initially lower, moisture. However, a few thunderstorms could produce
impactful downpours on saturated soils left over from last weekend's
historic rainfall.

Deeper moisture develops Saturday night and early Sunday. This is
expected to produce heavier and more widespread rainfall across
southeast UT and southwest CO Sunday and Monday, mostly below 10000
feet. While rivers are forecast to remain below action stage, a
growing concern lies in the potential for runoff around saturated
hillsides in the region. This could produce rock, mud, and debris
flows onto roadways, as well as flash flood prone burn scars, washes,
slot canyons, and arroyos. Early estimates predict an area of 1 to 2
inches of new rainfall for portions of southeast UT and southwest CO.

This is a preliminary forecast that hinges on slight shifts in a
strong moisture plume impacting the region. It also attempts to
capture the most statistically likely outcome, despite stronger and
weaker outlier predictions. Outdoor enthusiasts, motorists, and
residents of recent flood impacted areas are encouraged to remain
abreast of the developing forecast in the coming days.

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is occurring.

* WHEN...Until 645 PM MDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying

near San Pedro.

Lemitar, San Acacia, Laborcita, Luis Lopez and Chamizal.

properties.description:
ESFAFG

Areas of concern are between Nome and Council, particularity streams
and rivers draining the south aspects of the high elevation terrain
of the Seward Peninsula.

Rivers and streams in the Nome and Council area are already high
following rainfall over the weekend and early this week. Around 0.25
to 0.50" of additional rain is expected by the end of the week which
will keep water levels high. No flooding is expected but those along
the rivers and streams should be vigilant of the high water that is
expected through the end of the week.
